WoW: Forever

Protection Paladin

Shield tanking that generates threat from Holy damage rather than weapon damage, which makes it the only tank in the game that gears for Spell Power.

WoW: Forever · Tank · Updated October 31, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70707 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta closed on October 23 at level 30, so nothing above 30 was tested by players; talents and spells past 30 come from the launch client and Blizzard's posts. Talent tiers unlock at levels 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40. Blizzard's deep dive gives the point structure too: the one-point gold medal talents sit at 11, 21 and 31 points spent, joined in Forever by a new one at 16 points. Dual Specialization arrives at level 40.

No source had posted a level 30 build when this page was written, and the published level 20 builds no longer fit the tree. So both builds below are our own; no guide recommends them.

This page is written from Blizzard's Paladin Class Deep Dive, published October 15, and the launch client. These pages follow the hotfix Blizzard pushed to the launch realms on October 30, read from the game's hotfix data. Blizzard has not announced it, so it may still move before November 4.

Two kinds of caveat run through these pages and they do not mean the same thing. Something marked as ours is our own reasoning rather than a source's. A client or guide-site reading is a number Blizzard has not published.

A hover tooltip reads the base client, so it can lag a hotfix: where a tooltip and the prose differ, the prose is right. Seal of FurySeal of FuryLevel 10 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost40 ManaDuration30 secFills you with divine fury for 30 sec, causing melee attacks to deal an additional 6 Holy damage. While a shield is equipped, each attack also grants an absorb shield equal to 50% of the Holy damage dealt. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Unleashing this Seal's energy inflicts 32 to 34 Holy damage to an enemy and taunts the target to attack you for 4 sec. and Righteous FuryRighteous FuryLevel 10 · Spell · HolyCastInstantCost30% of base ManaDuration1800 secIncreases the threat generated by your Holy attacks by 90%. Lasts 1800 sec. are the two to watch here.

What Protection is for

Holding four enemies at once, and taunting without spending a talent point. Seal of FurySeal of FuryLevel 10 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost40 ManaDuration30 secFills you with divine fury for 30 sec, causing melee attacks to deal an additional 6 Holy damage. While a shield is equipped, each attack also grants an absorb shield equal to 50% of the Holy damage dealt. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Unleashing this Seal's energy inflicts 32 to 34 Holy damage to an enemy and taunts the target to attack you for 4 sec. is learned at level 10 and judging it taunts, which Blizzard confirms is baseline rather than a talent. ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. is baseline at 20 for every Paladin, and Righteous FuryRighteous FuryLevel 10 · Spell · HolyCastInstantCost30% of base ManaDuration1800 secIncreases the threat generated by your Holy attacks by 90%. Lasts 1800 sec. raises the threat of the Holy damage both of them deal, which is why Spell Power leads your stat priority.

Four is the number to plan pulls around. Blizzard redesigned ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. so it deals moderate damage to the first 4 enemies to enter it and very low damage to everyone else. Its stated reason is parity: a Paladin should generate reliable threat on four targets at a time, the same as a Warrior's Thunderclap, because Blizzard wants Forever to keep Classic Era's combat feel instead of sliding into the AoE-focused play of later expansions. Pull four, grind them down, and expect nothing dependable from the ring past that. Mana is the other limit.

Dungeon levelling is a mixed picture for this spec. It rested on ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec., its one source of damage to a whole pull, and one published guide called Forever's dungeon experience out as hurting this spec more than any other. Dungeon quests reward 50% less extra experience beyond normal quest values, a deliberate reduction in levelling speed, and kills inside dungeons pay about 20% more.

No source publishes a levelling score for any Paladin spec. Those experience figures and the guide's warning are what the sources say on levelling here.

Stat priority

Spell Power, then Hit, Stamina, Defense, Armor, Block, Intellect, Strength, Agility.

Spell Power first is correct here (ours, not a source's). In Forever a Paladin's threat is Holy damage: Seal of FurySeal of FuryLevel 10 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost40 ManaDuration30 secFills you with divine fury for 30 sec, causing melee attacks to deal an additional 6 Holy damage. While a shield is equipped, each attack also grants an absorb shield equal to 50% of the Holy damage dealt. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Unleashing this Seal's energy inflicts 32 to 34 Holy damage to an enemy and taunts the target to attack you for 4 sec., ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. and Holy StrikeHoly StrikeLevel 6 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost5 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown10 sec cooldownAn instant strike that causes 25% weapon damage plus an additional 11 to 14 as Holy damage., all amplified by Righteous FuryRighteous FuryLevel 10 · Spell · HolyCastInstantCost30% of base ManaDuration1800 secIncreases the threat generated by your Holy attacks by 90%. Lasts 1800 sec.. Hit earns its second place twice over, since PrecisionPrecisionTalent · Rank 1CastInstantImproves your chance to hit by 1%. now covers spells and a resisted Judgement is a failed taunt.

Righteous FuryRighteous FuryLevel 10 · Spell · HolyCastInstantCost30% of base ManaDuration1800 secIncreases the threat generated by your Holy attacks by 90%. Lasts 1800 sec. raises all your threat by 33%, and the threat of your Holy attacks by another 90%. Its tooltip shows only the 90%. Most of your threat still comes from the volume of Holy damage you put out yourself, which is the case for Spell Power restated.

Carry a shield and prefer a fast one-hander. The client's Seal of FurySeal of FuryLevel 10 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost40 ManaDuration30 secFills you with divine fury for 30 sec, causing melee attacks to deal an additional 6 Holy damage. While a shield is equipped, each attack also grants an absorb shield equal to 50% of the Holy damage dealt. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Unleashing this Seal's energy inflicts 32 to 34 Holy damage to an enemy and taunts the target to attack you for 4 sec. text makes the absorb conditional on having a shield equipped. Blizzard states the seal's bonus Holy damage is a constant amount per swing, unlike Seal of RighteousnessSeal of RighteousnessLevel 1 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost20 ManaDuration30 secFills the Paladin with holy spirit for 30 sec, granting each melee attack an additional 2.48 to 8.64 Holy damage. Slower weapons cause more Holy damage per swing. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time., and says outright that this favours a fast weapon while tanking. Swings per second scale both your threat and your absorb. Take mail over leather where the stats are close.

Leave spell power weapons alone below 20. Wowhead flags a trap here: a weapon with a heavy spell power roll carries roughly a 25% melee damage penalty, and you do not have the spell-power talents yet to make that trade pay off. A plain melee weapon out-damages it until you hit 20.

At level 60

Unknown, and one open question is specific: whether a 3-second conditional taunt can hold a raid boss. Blizzard's closing verdict is that Paladins can be highly effective tanks, with Swift JudgementSwift JudgementTalentCastInstantCooldown60 sec cooldownDurationUntil cancelledFinishes the remaining cooldown on your Judgement ability and reduces the Mana cost of your next Judgement by 100%. and Templar's BulwarkTemplar's BulwarkTalentCastInstantCost110 ManaCooldown300 sec cooldownDuration8 secWhen activated, this ability grants you an absorb shield equal to 100% of your maximum health for 8 sec. Applies Forbearance for 60 sec. Cannot be cast while Forbearance is active. as strong cooldowns tied to the Seal, Judgement and Forbearance systems, and baseline ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. plus Iron CreedIron CreedTalentCastInstantIncreases the threat generated by your Holy Strike ability by 30%. While Righteous Fury is active, Holy Strike also reduces your damage taken by 15% for 6 sec. giving more consistent control of the battlefield. Blizzard is equally plain about the gaps: no interrupt, no way to slow enemy movement, and limited range that Holy talents extend but never to a caster's reach. The four-target ceiling is design, not tuning, so do not expect it to lift.
